newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mt Edon says doesn't know buyer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mt Edon says doesn't know buyer.

text.p: Mount Edon Gold Mines (Australia) Ltd managing director Tony Brennan said on Wednesday he did not know who was behind the large trade in the company's shares.
At 2.10 p.m. (0310 GMT), Mount Edon shares were 63 cents or 43.45 percent up at A$2.08 with over nine million shares traded.
Mount Edon has about 73.5 million shares on issue.
"I don't really know. I guess we have got to wait and see," Brennan told Reuters. "It is either that (a takeover) or it is astute buying," Brennan said.

"The December quarterly was probably the best quarterly for a couple of years and we are getting some very encouraging drilling results out of Tarmoola just in recent days, some big hits," Brennan said.
On Friday Mount Edon reported record gold production for the three months to December 31, with output totaling 38,568 ounces, taking total six months output to 74,416 ounces.
He said he expected the group to produce about 130,000 ounces in the year to June 30, about double the previous year.
Mount Edon's main mines are Tarmoola and Nevoria, both in Western Australia.
Brennan said fund manager BT Australia held about 13 percent of Mount Edon, while fellow miner Westgold Resources has a 6.75 percent stake which it bought late last year.
He said Mount Edon had not spoken to Battle Mountain Gold since they held merger discussions about 15 months ago.
Most of the trade in Mount Edon was handled by Melbourne broker J.B Were and Son, which was seen buying at A$2.10.
The Perth-based miner has a market capitalisation of about A$155 million.
